source_text: Et hoc est propter quod maxime, miserantes Ecclesiarum ruinas, ad virorum prudentia illustrium provocamus examen, ut non quid dicatur, sed quid consequenter dicatur appareat. Si enim sub tali concilio disceptaretur, tibi utique non liceret, aut quod negaveras inferre, aut quod affirmaveras denegare; in libro vero tuo, quem nulla pudoris censura castigat, et quod Catholici dicunt, et quod Manichaei, confidenter agglomeras, hac sola opinione contentus, si respondisse dicaris; quid autem habeat ponderis oratio tua, quid constantiae, cogitare etiam ineptum putas.
pass_a_gloss: And this is the reason why especially, pitying the ruins of the Churches, we call forth to the examination of men illustrious by prudence, so that not what is said, but what is said consequently, may appear. For if it were disputed under such a council, it would certainly not be allowed to you either to infer what you had denied, or to deny what you had affirmed; but in your book, which no censure of shame chastens, you confidently heap together both what catholics say and what Manichaeans say, content with this opinion alone, if you are said to have answered; but what weight your speech has, what constancy, you think it even inept to consider.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: That is the chief reason why, grieving over the churches’ ruin, we appeal to examination by men distinguished for their wisdom: to reveal not merely what is said, but what is said consistently. If the dispute were heard before such a council, you would certainly not be allowed to assert what you had denied or deny what you had affirmed. But in your book, which no discipline of shame restrains, you boldly heap together what catholics say and what Manichaeans say. You are content with this one impression: that people say you have answered. You think it pointless even to consider what weight or consistency your argument possesses.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
